text: Did you know your heart
and mind are connected?
And they rely on each other?
When we're stressed, anxious
or feeling down,
our body releases hormones
that can raise blood pressure
and cause inflammation.
Too much of this, over time,
leads to strain on the heart
and increases your risk of developing heart disease.
And it's a two way relationship.
Living with a heart condition
can impact how we feel emotionally.
It is normal to feel sadness and worry
after experiencing a heart event, known as cardiac blues.
This usually passes within a few weeks or months.
If the blues stick around,
it can lead to depression and anxiety
that needs professional help.
The good news?
Taking small steps can make a big difference.
When you move your body,
connect with others,
eat heart healthy foods,
and pause to recharge,
you're giving both your heart and your mind
the support they need to thrive.
So remember, caring for your mind helps your heart too.
Talk to your doctor and visit the Heart Foundation website
for tools and support to care
for both your mental health and heart health.
